literal: Trusting those who have no relations, avoid; for they, attachment do not have, will not feel ashamed of disgrace.
translation: Avoid choosing or trusting those who have no family ties; since they have no attachments, they will not fear disgrace.
modern: உறவினர்கள் இல்லாதவர்களைத் தேர்ந்தெடுத்து நம்புவதைத் தவிர்க்க வேண்டும்; ஏனெனில், அவர்களுக்குப் பற்று இல்லாததால் அவர்கள் பழிக்கு அஞ்சமாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet warns a leader against employing or trusting individuals who have no family ties or social attachments. The key words are 'பற்று இலர்' (those without attachments) and 'நாணார் பழி' (those who do not fear disgrace). A person with family and social connections is naturally restrained by the fear of bringing shame upon their loved ones. In contrast, someone completely detached from such relationships lacks this moral anchor and is more likely to commit dishonorable acts without any fear of public blame. Therefore, choosing such people for responsible positions must be avoided.
